The declared microscopic class has a nearest-neighbor one-dimensional spin energy, a boundary seed, and a kinetic constraint that prevents bulk spin changes or creation of additional fronts. Starting all-minus, the accessible states are prefixes with one interface, indexed by n. This is a bijection of the declared reachable state space, not elimination of an exponentially populated set of configurations. With a target before the far boundary, heat-bath rates give a special boundary birth a=lambda_0, retreat b=mu_1, and constant interior birth lambda and retreat mu. The visible response uses negative h for its very long adverse threshold-crossing examples and separately reports positive-h boundary escape. These are different physical regimes.

For arbitrary positive birth-death rates, d_0=1/lambda_0 and d_n=(1+mu_n*d_(n-1))/lambda_n give the mean to target m as sum_(n=0)^(m-1) d_n. First-passage transforms follow g_0(s)=lambda_0/(s+lambda_0), g_n(s)=lambda_n/(s+lambda_n+mu_n-mu_n*g_(n-1)(s)), F_0(s)=product g_n(s). These preserve repeated retreats and physical residence time. They are standard finite-chain constructions.

Theorem1.1 applies to a continuous-time birth-death generator on0,...,d, start0, absorbingd, other birth and death rates positive.
